_comment: HywMill M5 politics. Standing uses Millénaire's combined reputation (village + culture): boycott -1024, hire 4096, friend of the village 8192, one of us 32768. Outlaw: grievance >= outlaw AND reputation <= boycott, or a killing inside the village in peacetime (immediate). Pardon: grievance < pardon AND reputation > boycott. A status earned by reputation is kept down to threshold x keepFactor. Grievance: weight x insideFactor (inside the village) x selfDefenseFactor (the victim struck first), halving every halfLifeDays. Favor is earned only by service (no trade source) and capped. Formal pardon (weregild): perGrievance reputation per grievance point above the pardon line, plus killFee while a peacetime killing is pending; refused unless reputation stays above the boycott line after paying. Apology (not outlaws): apologyPerGrievance Millénaire deniers per grievance point (64 = 1 denier argent) settles the grievance at once; reputation is untouched; 0 disables it. Diplomacy (envoys): a logistic success chance from bias[kind] + standing, relation, conflict, culture, distance, strength and repeated-attempt terms; delta is the relation change on success (Millenaire scale, +-jitter); envoys travel travelPer200 ticks per 200 blocks (at least minTravel); a truce holds the relation at truceFloor for truceDays; sow discord is Sworn-only with player and pair cooldowns, a rising Favor cost and exposure chance. Requests: detachments (Patron 4, Sworn 8; player-following escorts are deferred to a later phase) are lent garrison units the village can spare under its raid rule (minHome, kept sentry pairs and reserve); willingness falls with casualties on the player's errands and rises with Favor; Favor is paid on acceptance and lost per soldier killed on the errand. Raid counsel (post-M5): a player on campaign with a village (at war) may suggest a raid on the enemy from the Politics screen; it costs pointCost Millénaire diplomacy points with the village and has a cooldown per player; the village agrees with chance[standing], times tooStrongFactor when the target defends with at least twice the raiding strength (Millénaire's own limit), within minChance..maxChance; on agreement Millénaire plans the raid its usual way (announcement, raid a day later, the garrison's raid share with it). Sieges (post-M5, docs/siege-design.md): HYW-only expeditions of a garrison against a village at war with it (the garrison no longer joins Millénaire raids): a host (commitFraction of the garrison, keeping minHome) musters, marches stowed (marchPer100 ticks per 100 blocks), and fights before the target when a player is there (fought until one side is down to 20% of its soldiers at the start (breakFraction/routFraction), or battleTicks = 15 min, then the side that kept the larger share wins) or is decided off-screen after waitTicks by strength (P = H^e/(H^e+D^e), e = 2, Millénaire defenders count millenaireWeight; loserLoss/winnerLoss of HYW units die). The loser pays tribute by its tier: levyShare levy points per 4096 deniers move to the winner, playerShare of it is paid to the winner's helpers (players on campaign with it near the battle), who also gain helperRep reputation and SIEGE_VICTORY Favor. Patron/Sworn campaigners can counsel a siege (counselChance, counselPoints diplomacy points, counselCooldown); villages at war also launch sieges themselves (aiDailyChance per day when host/defense >= aiMinRatio, aiCooldown after one). War arsenal (post-M5): a village that goes to war (declared or declared on) raises engines[tier] siege engines drawn from types (catapults and springalds; trebuchets are too big for village defense) (a stronghold draws one from strongholdTypes), each with a siege engineer, at its defending position; engines lost in the war are not replaced; survivors stand down when the village is at peace again and the next war brings a fresh arsenal; they march with the village's sieges (set up behind the host) and in off-screen sieges each weighs engineStrength and cancels fortCut of the target's fortification bonus. No gunpowder engines. War and peace counsel (post-M5): a Patron or Sworn player may suggest from the Politics screen that a village declare war on another (council chance warChance[standing] x (1 - relation/200) x 2 x its strength share, capped at x1.25) or make peace with an enemy (peaceChance[standing] x (1.5 - its strength share), then the enemy accepts with the other side's strength share, within enemyMin..enemyMax; share = ours^e/(ours^e + theirs^e), strength = garrison at home + weighted Millenaire defenders + engines, x fortification); each costs warPoints/peacePoints diplomacy points and a cooldown. A declared war starts at once (relations set to warRelation); a peace, and every finished siege when peaceAfterSiege (the loser sues for peace), sets both relations to peaceRelation and ends the war at once, calling any host between them home. Mobilization (post-M5): a village that is not a stronghold fills its garrison to its current target when it goes to war, at no levy cost, with troops at equipment level max(equipmentFloor, regular - equipmentDrop); they serve as ordinary units and go home when the village is at peace again. Relief forces (post-M5): when any siege is launched (by a player's counsel or a village's own decision), each village with a relation of at least minRelation to the besieged village (and at peace with it, garrison at home >= minGarrison) promises relief with chance, at most maxHelpers per siege; when the attackers march it sends shareMin..shareMax of its garrison at home by forced march, arriving after minTicks..maxTicks (usually before the attackers), spread round the village; its faction and the attacker's are HOSTILE while it is out and it counts among the defenders (also off-screen). On the way it may be ambushed (ambushChance: ambushLossMin..ambushLossMax of it killed, a real loss; with routChance the rest flee home and none arrive) or lose its way (lostChance: lostMin..all of it never arrives, unharmed, back home). It goes home when the siege ends. Cultures patch fields.
